The University of Rhode Island College of Nursing’s Accelerated Online R.N. to B.S. program is dedicated to providing an education that will broaden your view of the world and create opportunities to transform healthcare in your own community. Permission to retake the course will be granted on a space-available basis only. Even if successfully repeated, the initial grade remains on record as the first unsuccessful attempt. There are no further allowances for repeating a NUR course, and any subsequent NUR coursework of C- or below will result in dismissal. If the student should achieve a C- or less in two NUR courses in a single session or semester, he or she will be immediately dismissed from the College of Nursing. A total of 120 credits is required to earn a B.S. in Nursing. This includes program specific courses as well as general education requirements. R.N. to B.S. COURSES CASC Bill 2025-2026-01A At the September 30, 2025 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. TEMPORARY COURSES COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES BIO232X | How Genes Work, Spring 2026 (4 crs.) The class will review the major steps in gene expression and cell signaling by summarizing research focused on biological processes and by building physical and digital models of the processes (Lec. 3, Rec. 1) Pre: BIO101 or permission of instructor. SUS102X (EVS102X) | Introduction to Sustainability, Spring 2026 (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (GEO) EVS102X. Introduces sustainability science through the integrated study of Earth, ecological, and human systems, exploring global challenges such as climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity loss, and resource management through systems thinking and real-world solutions. (Lec. 3) FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES AAF205 | Early African Civilizations, Spring 2026 (3 crs.) This course looks at Africa’s ancient empires and early African attempts at innovation and environmental adaption. It also explores religion and what constitutes African theology and nature- related worship system. (Lec. 3)

AAF367 | Comics, Graphic Novels and Black Culture, Spring 2026 (3 crs.) This class provides an introduction to the history, culture, and art of Africana comics and to the various methodologies that define the emerging academic area of comics studies. (Lec. 3) AAF401 | The Earl N.
Smith III Cabo Verde Study Abroad Program, Summer 2026 (3 crs.) This course is a three-credit study abroad exploring the history of Cabo Verde.
Students will travel to three of the country’s ten islands and visit museums and cultural sites. (Lec. 3) Pre: GPA of 2.5, sophomore standing.
AAF407 | Hip Hop as Culture, Social Commentary and Praxis, Spring 2026 (3 crs.) This course uses Hip Hop to analyze rebellion, resistance and social issues through an Africana Studies lens.
The course is organized around the famous statement: “Emancipate yourselves from mental slavery.” (Lec. 3) Pre: MUS208(AAF208).
Not for graduate credit.

FLM320 | 20Somethings TV, Spring 2026 (4 crs.) Introduction to producing media through creation of weekly TV talk show segments in the broadcast studio, developing expertise in production roles and participating in the delivery of weekly content. (Studio) Pre: FLM101 and FLM110, sophomore standing.
COURSE MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES GWS340 (AAF340) | Black Feminisms, Summer 2026 Add in-person modality, cross-list with AAF, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (GWS) AAF340.
This course explores the paradigm-shifting contributions of women of African descent to discourses of feminism. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: GWS150 or AAF201 or AAF355/HIS355 or permission on instructor.
COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING CHE445 | Chemical Engineering Laboratory I, Fall 2026 Change title, prerequisites (2 crs.) Quantitative studies illustrating chemical engineering principles.
Emphasis on report writing and the interpretation of experimental data. (Lab. 6) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in CHE348 or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
CHE446 | Chemical Engineering Laboratory II, Fall 2026 Change Title (2 crs.) Quantitative studies illustrating chemical engineering principles.

Emphasis on report writing and the interpretation of experimental data. (Lab. 6) Pre: CHE348 or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.

COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES AVS300 | Winter Dairy Travel Course, Winter 2026 Change temporary course to permanent (1 cr.) Extended field trip to dairy farms and dairy-related businesses with students and faculty from other New England land-grant universities.
The course includes discussion sessions, case study, problem solving, and journal reports with student presentations. (Lab. 1) Pre: AVS323 or permission of instructor.
S/U Only.
AVS400 | Advanced Small Farm Management, Spring 2026 Change temporary course to permanent (4 crs.) Students integrate knowledge of husbandry with business/accounting principles, site - planning, assistance programs, and labor management of a small farm.
Farm design, machinery skills, feed calculations, manure, and people management. (Lec. 3, Lab. 1) Pre: AVS102 and AVS275; Completed or concurrent enrollment in AVS304, AVS332; AVS212 or AVS412; AVS323 or AVS324; senior standing or by permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
MAF491 | Special Problems, Fall 2026 Change credits from fixed to variable (1-6 crs.) Individual guidance in major readings and methods of research. (Independent Study) Pre: permission of chairperson.

Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES HDF340 | Introduction to Early Intervention, Summer 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Orientation to Early Intervention services for families with children ages birth to three with developmental delays.
The course describes various disabilities, introduces family-centered service approaches, and examines early identification methods. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit or concurrent enrollment in HDF306, minimum sophomore standing.
